title: Test the npm Package, Not Just the Monorepo
why_read: A focused, technically substantive post about a subtle but real class of bugs where a library passes its own tests yet fails silently once installed as a real npm package in a consumer's application.
analysis: The author, who maintains a tracing/observability library called AgentInspect, explains how duplicate copies of a module can exist in a dependency tree even when the tree looks deduplicated, causing an adapter to look at a different in-memory context instance than the one the real application is using. This causes silent capture failures that unit tests checking only return values would never catch, which is a genuinely important and under-discussed testing gap. The post describes building a separate 'installed package' smoke test against real published versions and a real MCP SDK version to catch this class of bug specifically. This is a solid, specific lesson in packaging and runtime-identity pitfalls that is broadly applicable beyond this one library.
